news.title: Alternative tournament plan outside World Cup: Is FIFA facing a split?
news.lede: Rarely has world football witnessed a scene quite like this: FIFA’s president facing an open vote of no confidence from three of his own vice-presidents, with the dispute escalating to discussions about an alternative tournament to the World Cup. Under Gianni Infantino’s leadership, a failed attempt to sell stakes in the commercial rights to FIFA competitions is no longer merely a dispute over a business decision. It has evolved into an open confrontation over power, trust and control of the global game. The heads of UEFA, the AFC and Concacaf have accused Infantino of breaching their trust through what they describe as a “deceptive” process and have raised the prospect of a change in leadership.

news.title: Infantino's offer: take Mexico out of Concacaf and put it into Conmebol in exchange for its vote
news.lede: The FMF would have received a proposal from Gianni Infantino: he would help Mexico leave Concacaf to join Conmebol, in exchange for guaranteeing him their vote in the next FIFA presidential election. This information was revealed by journalist Martín del Palacio, who stated that the support of the Mexican Football Federation (FMF) would be key for the Swiss official to remain at the helm of the highest governing body of world football. However, the change of confederation would not be easy, as it would require approval through different filters. Despite this, in Mexico they view favorably an option that would happen only and exclusively if the current president remains in office.

news.title: Gianni Infantino: Division over Fifa president shown in map of support and opposition
news.lede: Gianni Infantino's previously untouchable status at the top of world football is now under significant pressure. As recently as mid-July, Gianni Infantino was considered a shoo-in to be re-elected as Fifa president next March. All but a handful of Fifa's 210 members had endorsed his bid for a fourth term in charge of world football, and he faced no meaningful challenge from any quarter. But that picture looks very different now, after two weeks of relentless fallout to his now-abandoned plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup and other competitions to private investors.
